mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC's own trajectory shows three consecutive weeks of stabilization followed by a 2.9-point jump in the latest week, indicating accumulating consumer momentum that should persist and push retail mobility higher over the next four weeks via habit reinforcement.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -31.0 to -28.1 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's mean over the next 28 days is not higher than its mean over the last 28 days despite the observed week-over-week uptick.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in TRANSIT mobility beyond a 3-point weekly threshold signals renewed commuting and errand-running behavior that mechanically drives retail footfall higher within two weeks, as transit use is a necessary precondition for most retail visits in dense Tokyo districts.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 3 points week-on-week for at least one week in the snapshot
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -35.1 to -33.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the two weeks following a TRANSIT improvement exceeding the 3-point threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show simultaneous week-over-week improvement, the compounded return of commuting and office-based routines creates incidental retail demand (lunch, errands, after-work shopping) that amplifies RETAIL_REC recovery beyond what either series predicts alone.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean does not exceed its trailing mean even though both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated in double digits (12-13%) across all four weeks, indicating that stay-at-home policy compliance under the ongoing state of emergency is still binding; as long as RESIDENTIAL stays above 10%, discretionary retail trips will remain suppressed regardless of minor upticks elsewhere.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 10 percent for all four snapshot weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 12.1 and 13.4 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean rises above its trailing mean while RESIDENTIAL remains above 10 percent throughout.

mechanism_narrative: Large week-over-week swings in PARKS mobility (e.g., the drop to -34.9 then rebound to -23.1) indicate weather- or event-driven outdoor substitution; when PARKS visits spike sharply, households reallocate limited discretionary outings away from retail toward open-air recreation, depressing RETAIL_REC in the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -34.9 to -23.1 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week immediately following a PARKS increase exceeding 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-September marks the approach of Tokyo's autumn shopping season (back-to-school, early year-end promotions) and the scheduled end of the extended state-of-emergency period; historically this seasonal transition combined with policy fatigue produces a structural uplift in retail mobility over the following four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2021-09-15 near the end of the declared emergency period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean fails to exceed its trailing mean despite the calendar proximity to the emergency's scheduled end.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-week decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility (greater than 1 point drop) signals an early loosening of self-imposed or policy-driven confinement behavior, which should translate into a near-term rise in RETAIL_REC within one week as suppressed demand is released.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by more than 1 point week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 13.4 to 12.1 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a RESIDENTIAL drop exceeding 1 point.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stayed flat to slightly positive while RETAIL_REC remains deeply negative, suggesting households are substituting discretionary retail trips with essential-only shopping; if this gap widens further, consumers will continue prioritizing essential errands over discretionary retail, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed near 0-3 percent while RETAIL_REC stayed near -28 to -31 percent across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward mean rises even as the gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC widens further.
